summary: August Wilhelm von Schlegel (1767–1845) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne, and later under Alexander Hamilton and Antoine-Léonard de Chézy, holding chairs at Jena, Breslau, and the University of Bonn.

Auguste Barth (1834–1916) was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Strasbourg. He taught at Collège de Saverne (1856–1861) and was a member of the Institut de France and the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences.
Auguste Comte (1798–1857) was a philosopher who studied at Lycée Joffre until 1814 and subsequently at the École polytechnique from 1814 to 1816.

Augustus Frederic Rudolf Hoernle (1841–1918) was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He served as Director of Calcutta Madrasa (~1881–1899) and was Philological Secretary at The Asiatic Society in 1891.

Active in Tibetology and other fields, Aung San Suu Kyi studied at Lady Shri Ram College, the University of Delhi, St Hugh's College, and SOAS University of London. She also held a post at the United Nations (~1969–1971).

Axel Klein (born 1968) is a Japanology scholar who studied and worked at the University of Bonn. He later held posts at the German Institute for Japanese Studies and the University of Duisburg-Essen, where he became professor in 2012.

Axel Michaels (born 1949), an Indologist and scholar of religious studies, earned his Promotion at Hamburg and Habilitation at Kiel. He directed the Nepal Research Centre and held professorships at the University of Bern and the University of Heidelberg.

Ayu Khandro (1839–1953) was active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Nyala Pema Dündul, Chokgyur Lingpa, and Drodul Pawo Dorje, and taught Namkhai Norbu.

Ayya Khema (1923–1997) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies teacher. She studied under Ajahn Singtong, Ajahn Maha Bua, Laurence Khantipalo Mills, and Matara Sri Ñāṇarāma, and taught at Buddha-Haus from 1989.

B. Alan Wallace (born 1950) works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied under Carl Bielefeldt at Stanford (Ph.D.) and several traditional Tibetan masters, and held posts at IHET, Rabten Choeling, and UCSB.

B. N. Goswamy (1933–2023) was an Indian art historian and Indologist. He studied at Panjab University (~1950–1961), served in the Indian Administrative Service (~1956–1958), and later held a post at Panjab University from ~1965 to 1993.

B. N. K. Sharma (1909–2005) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied under Satyadhyana Tirtha and at Madras, held posts at Annamalai, Rajah's, Poornaprajna, and Dr. A. V. Baliga colleges, and retired from Ramnarain Ruia College.

B. R. Ambedkar (1891–1956), active in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, studied at Columbia, LSE, and London under John Dewey and Edwin Cannan, among others. He was professor at Sydenham College and principal of Government Law College.

B. R. Gopal (1930–1997) was an Indologist and historian. He was attested as Technical Research Assistant at the Archaeological Survey of India (1964), Epigraphical Assistant at Government Epigraphist for India (1965), and Epigraphist at Epigraphia Carnatica (1974).

Baatr Kitinov works in history, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He received a Ph.D. in World History from Moscow State University and serves as Associate Professor of the Department of World History at Peoples' Friendship University of Russia.

Baburam Saksena (1897–1989) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University in 1921 and served as Vice-Chancellor of Pt. Ravishankar Shukla University from ~1965 to 1968.

Bahadur Chand Chhabra (1908–1994) worked in Indology and archaeology. He earned a doctorate at Leiden and held posts at the Archaeological Survey of India, Government Epigraphist for India, and Panjab University.
Baiei Henmi (1891–1977) was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology scholar. He studied at Tokyo Imperial University (~1915–1918) and later held a post at Tama Art University (~1953–1965).

Baihui Wu (1919–2014) was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Visva-Bharati University, Peking University as Professor of Sanskrit, the Institute of Philosophy, and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences.

Baij Nath Puri (1916–1996) was an Indologist and historian who earned his doctorate at Oxford. He served as Professor and Head of Ancient Indian History and Archaeology at the University of Lucknow from ~1945 to 1976.
